target.title: fix(irc): hide tool traces from inbound replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where IRC users could receive internal tool-trace banners when an assistant reply was sent from the inbound message callback. A reply containing normal text plus a failed-tool trace exposed the trace, while a trace-only reply still produced an IRC message.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inbound IRC reply path now reuses the same assistant-visible plain-text sanitizer already declared by the IRC outbound adapter, before attachment links are formatted. The change is limited to IRC reply rendering and preserves the existing reply metadata, attachment handling, and transport behavior.

## User Impact

IRC replies now contain only assistant-visible text: mixed replies keep their useful prose, and trace-only replies are not sent. Ordinary IRC assistant replies are unchanged.

## Evidence

AI-assisted.

### Before and premise

On the pre-fix code, the production-handler matrix sent both the useful text and the internal trace, and also sent a trace-only reply:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/irc/src/inbound.behavior.test.ts

mixed assistant text:
expected ["Done."]
received ["Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"]

trace-only assistant text:
expected []
received ["⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"]
```

`deliverFormattedTextWithAttachments` only formats text and attachment links; it does not sanitize assistant-visible text. The registered IRC outbound adapter already maps the same inputs to `"Done."` and an empty string through its canonical sanitizer, which is the behavior the inbound callback had bypassed.

### After: real IRC transport proof

I ran a real ngIRCd 26.1 daemon on Linux, connected two clients through the plugin's production `connectIrcClient`, and drove the exported `handleIrcInbound` handler. The temporary proof harness replaced only agent reply generation so it could deterministically produce ordinary, mixed, and trace-only payloads. Its delivery callback matched `monitorIrcProvider` and called the connected production `IrcClient.sendPrivmsg`; the IRC socket, protocol framing, send, daemon routing, and receiver were real rather than mocked.

Daemon start and proof command:

```text
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/tmp/ngircd-proof/pkg/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu \
  /tmp/ngircd-proof/pkg/usr/sbin/ngircd -n \
  -f /tmp/ngircd-proof/ngircd.conf

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/irc/src/inbound.live-proof.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

The receiver observed the following messages. The 1.5-second quiet window after the trace-only case produced no third message:

```text
ordinary received: ["The pipeline has 3 open deals."]
mixed received: ["The pipeline has 3 open deals.","Done."]
trace-only received after quiet window: ["The pipeline has 3 open deals.","Done."]

✓ delivers only assistant-visible inbound replies over ngIRCd
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
```

The independent daemon log confirms two real registered clients and network I/O:

```text
Accepted connection 7 from "127.0.0.1:34992"
User "ocp5568298r!~ocp5568298r@127.0.0.1" registered (connection 7).
Accepted connection 8 from "127.0.0.1:34996"
User "ocp5568298s!~ocp5568298s@127.0.0.1" registered (connection 8).
Connection 8 ... closed (in: 0.2k, out: 1.5k).
Connection 7 ... closed (in: 0.1k, out: 1.6k).
ngIRCd done, served 2 connections.
```

The ordinary reply is the negative control: it proves the same network harness receives messages when the sanitizer should preserve content. The mixed case proves only user-facing prose crosses the transport, and the trace-only case proves no IRC message is emitted.

The focused and complete IRC plugin tests also pass:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/irc/src/inbound.behavior.test.ts extensions/irc/src/channel.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       12 passed (12)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/irc/src
Test Files  16 passed (16)
Tests       98 passed (98)
```

Targeted `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` pass. `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode uncommitted` completed with `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`.

Limit: the real IRC daemon ran on localhost without TLS; no third-party public network was used. This proof exercises the final production IRC socket and daemon routing behavior without sending test traffic to a public channel.
